lessons: cycles 1-12 (owner review 2026-08-14, the big one): The portfolio drifted into CLOSET INDEXING and nobody noticed because the returns looked fine. The cause was a self-contradicting brief: 'maximize long-term profit' paired with rules that mandate becoming the index. Lesson: diversification rules and a profit-maximizing mandate pull in opposite directions, and when they conflict the rules win silently. Every dollar must express a view.

cycles 10-12 (owner review 2026-08-14): The four-cycle no-trade stretch was misdiagnosed as an over-strict scoring bar. The actual failure was a FUNNEL of only three stale candidates (LIN/AMT/CAT) re-checked cycle after cycle, with zero new names screened. Lesson: when nothing passes the bar, screen more candidates; never lower the bar.

cycle 13: A restructure that sells several positions in one cash-account cycle runs into T+1 settlement — sale proceeds are not spendable same-day. Plan buy sequencing around settled buying power, not gross cash, and don't be surprised when 'cash %' looks high right after a big sell day; check buying_power specifically, not just the cash field, before sizing buys.

cycle 13: The most durable candidates on a multi-cycle watchlist (AMT, 13 cycles of 'not yet') can still eventually clear the technical bar — AMT's SMA breakout this cycle is a reminder not to drop a name just because it's been patient; the discipline of waiting for a real signal instead of a stale re-check was the point of keeping it on the list at all.

cycle 14: CAT's fundamental thesis reversed back at Cycle 10 (record backlog) but the stock has now fallen for six straight weeks anyway, round-tripping well past where the Cycle 10/11 'wait for consolidation' call expected. Lesson: a reversed fundamental thesis with a stubbornly broken chart can stay broken far longer than expected — the technical-confirmation requirement (not just the fundamental read) is doing real work here, not just being cautious for its own sake.

cycle 14: Building two new research candidates into a full 5-score writeup (not just a hunch) surfaced a clean decline (HD, reaffirmed-not-raised guidance plus a named headwind) alongside a clean buy (UNP, raised guidance plus a genuine new-sector fit) — the score discipline works precisely because it lets two similar-looking 'beat' stories land on opposite sides of the bar.

cycle 15: A high score alone (CQP, 20/25) is not sufficient to buy — cash was already mid-band (3.4%, inside the 2-5% target) rather than piled up above it, so there was no idle-cash mandate and no clean funding source without breaching the cash floor or trimming an in-target, thesis-intact holding. The cash-target rule binds both directions: it blocks buying when there's nothing to deploy, not just when there's too much sitting idle.

cycle 16: A new candidate barely clearing the 18/25 bar (DE, weak on valuation) doesn't automatically deserve a forced trim-and-rotate when a stronger, already-vetted candidate (CQP, 20/25) is sitting unbought in the same queue — screen order isn't buy order; work down the backlog by conviction, not by whichever name was researched most recently. Also: HD reaffirming (not raising) guidance for a second straight quarter is itself information — a name can sit on the watchlist through multiple real beats and still never clear the bar if the specific missing ingredient (a guidance raise) never shows up.

cycle 17: The cash-target band is a percentage, but the funding decision is about absolute dollars — $35.64 sits mid-2-5% band yet can't fund any ~$90-110 position regardless of what the band says. A second 20/25 candidate (PGR) joining CQP in the unfunded queue, with no over-cap position available to trim, means the backlog itself is becoming the binding constraint; three straight constrained cycles is the threshold past which a deliberate trim-to-fund call (not a forced one) becomes worth considering, not indefinite deferral.

cycle 18: The recurring cash-constrained backlog (CQP/PGR unfunded for 2-4 cycles) was misdiagnosed as a funding problem to solve by trimming a laggard — position count (13, 12 single names) is already 2 over the 8-10 single-name target band, so the real constraint is that the book is full, not cash-poor. Checking Cycle 17's own suggested trim candidates (GOOGL, NEE) closely, neither had a broken thesis to justify cutting. A passing score (MU, 18/25) is necessary but not sufficient when there's no open slot and no invalidation trigger has freed one — decline on construction grounds, don't manufacture an exit.
